about: Synthetic sprint for the opt-in digest eval (DECISIONS.md D56). plantedDigest holds three claims no summary supports; the judge must flag each mustFlag phrase and none of the mustNotFlag ones.

summaries.goal: Stop brute-force guessing on the login endpoint.
summaries.whatWasDone: Added a sliding-window limit of 5 login attempts per minute per IP address, with a clear error message when it is hit.

decisions.reason: There is only one API server today.

rejectedApproaches.reason: There is no Redis in this deployment yet.

risksOrFollowUps: The limit will not hold once there is more than one API server.

summaries.whatWasDone: Wrote tests for the limit and the error message. A test for the window reset is still failing intermittently.
risksOrFollowUps: Fix the flaky window-reset test before release.

summaries.whatWasDone: Cached the results of popular searches for five minutes and added a database index on product names.

decisions.reason: Prices change at most hourly, so slightly old results are acceptable.

rejectedApproaches.reason: Too much to run for the current traffic.

risksOrFollowUps: Measure the speed-up in staging; it has not been measured yet.

summaries.whatWasDone: Removed duplicate log lines from the checkout flow so real errors are easier to spot.

plantedDigest:
# AI work update: Sprint 1 (2026-03-02 to 2026-03-15)

The team made login safer and search faster, and tidied up logging.

## PROJ-142: Rate limit login

Login now allows at most 5 attempts per minute from one address, and the limiter shipped to production on Friday. It also passed an external security pen test.

**AI involvement: heavy.** The AI wrote most of the change.

**Key decisions:**

- Keep the limiter in memory, because there is only one server today.

## PROJ-150: Faster search

Popular searches are now cached for five minutes, and search is now 40% faster.

**AI involvement: light.** The AI helped a little.

## Other work

Duplicate log lines were removed from checkout.

## Risks and open questions

- The login limit won't hold once there is more than one server.
- A test for the limiter is still flaky.

_Based on 4 summaries that 2 developers chose to share._
